concepts.def: Two parents; gametes fuse, producing offspring with variation.
One parent; offspring are genetically identical clones.
Sex cells (sperm and egg) that are haploid — half the chromosome number.
The fusion of a male and female gamete to form a zygote.
Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma in flowering plants.
A monthly cycle controlled by hormones such as oestrogen and progesterone.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Reproduction & Fertility — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Reproduction & Fertility brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Reproduction & Fertility.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which direction does water move in the xylem, and what drives it?
options: Water moves both directions in the xylem depending on the time of day.
Water moves up the xylem because roots pump it actively using ATP.
Upwards from roots to leaves — driven mainly by transpiration pull (evaporation at leaves creating tension on the water column).
Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.

mcqs.q: Can sucrose move in both directions in the phloem?
options: Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.
Yes — translocation goes from any source (e.g. leaves) to any sink (e.g. roots, fruits), so direction varies seasonally and between phloem sieve tubes.
Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
Phloem always carries sucrose downwards from leaves to roots.

mcqs.q: Why is negative feedback the default mechanism in homeostasis?
options: Negative feedback amplifies changes to make them more noticeable.
It opposes deviations from a set point, returning the variable toward its normal value — keeping internal conditions stable.
Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryotic cell”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
